title: Specific Gravity of Rock Specimen
variable_meanings: W_dry = Dry weight of rock specimen in air; W_submerged = Apparent submerged weight of specimen in water.
when_to_use: When determining relative density or porosity of rock cores from Archimedes immersion tests.
common_traps: Denominator must be (W_dry - W_submerged), which represents the buoyant force (weight of displaced water), not W_submerged alone.

title: USBM Ground Vibration Attenuation Law (PPV)
variable_meanings: PPV = Peak Particle Velocity (mm/s); D = Distance from blast to structure (m); Q = Maximum explosive charge per delay (kg); K, beta = Site geological transmission constants; (D / sqrt(Q)) = Scaled distance.
units: PPV in mm/s, D in m, Q in kg, Scaled distance in m/kg^0.5
when_to_use: Calculating maximum allowable blast charge per delay to ensure vibration limits at surface structures are not exceeded.
common_traps: Q is explosive charge per delay (delay interval), NOT the total explosive charge of the entire round!
example_problem: D = 100 m, Q = 25 kg => Scaled Distance = 100 / sqrt(25) = 20 m/kg^0.5.

title: Apparent Dip to True Dip Trigonometric Relation
variable_meanings: alpha = Apparent dip angle; theta = True dip angle; gamma = Angle between true dip direction and apparent dip direction.
when_to_use: When converting between apparent dip measured in a roadway crosscut and the true dip of the geological seam.
common_traps: True dip (theta) is always greater than or equal to any apparent dip (alpha). If calculated alpha > theta, the formula was applied inverted.
example_problem: True dip theta = 30 deg, gamma = 45 deg => tan(alpha) = tan(30) * cos(45) = 0.5774 * 0.7071 = 0.4082 => alpha = 22.2 deg.

title: Mohr-Coulomb Shear Failure Criterion
variable_meanings: tau = Shear stress at failure (MPa); c = Cohesion (MPa); sigma_n = Normal stress acting on failure plane (MPa); phi = Angle of internal friction (degrees).
units: tau, c, sigma_n in MPa; phi in degrees
when_to_use: Determining shear strength and stability of rock joints, rock slopes, or underground pillar failure envelopes.
common_traps: The angle of the failure plane with the major principal stress plane is (45 + phi/2), not just phi.

title: Tributary Area Theory (Pillar Stress & Extraction Ratio)
variable_meanings: sigma_p = Average vertical stress on coal pillar (MPa); sigma_v = In-situ vertical overburden stress (MPa) = gamma * H; R = Areal extraction ratio; w = Pillar width (m); B = Gallery width (m); H = Depth from surface (m); gamma = Unit weight of overburden (MN/m3).
units: sigma_p, sigma_v in MPa; w, B, H in meters
when_to_use: Estimating vertical stress concentration on square or rectangular coal pillars in Bord and Pillar workings.
common_traps: Ensure w is the pillar core width and (w+B) is the center-to-center pillar distance. R = 1 - (w / (w+B))^2 for square pillars.

title: Atkinson's Law of Mine Ventilation Pressure
formula_latex: P = R Q^2 = \frac{k S Q^2}{A^3} = \frac{k O L Q^2}{A^3}
variable_meanings: P = Frictional pressure drop (Pa); R = Airway resistance (Ns^2/m^8); k = Friction factor (Ns^2/m^4); S = Rubbing surface = O * L (m2); O = Roadway perimeter (m); L = Roadway length (m); A = Cross-sectional area (m2); Q = Airflow volume (m3/s).
units: P in Pa (N/m2), R in Ns^2/m^8, Q in m3/s, A in m2, S in m2
when_to_use: Calculating ventilation pressure losses, fan head requirements, and equivalent orifices for mine airways.
common_traps: Notice A is raised to the 3rd power in the denominator! If area is halved, resistance increases by 2^3 = 8 times.

title: Mine Air Power & Fan Input Power
variable_meanings: P_air = Useful air power output (kW); P = Total fan pressure (Pa); Q = Total air quantity handled (m3/s); eta_fan = Fan mechanical efficiency; eta_motor = Motor electrical efficiency.
units: Power in kW, P in Pa, Q in m3/s
when_to_use: Sizing mine ventilation fan motors and estimating electrical energy consumption costs.
common_traps: Do not forget to divide by 1000 to convert Watts into kW. When efficiencies are given, divide by efficiency to find input power.

title: Net Present Value (NPV) of Mining Project
variable_meanings: CF_t = Net annual cash inflow in year t ($ or Rs); r = Discount rate / Cost of capital (decimal); C_0 = Initial capital investment / CAPEX; N = Mine operating life (years).
when_to_use: Evaluating mine feasibility, investment decisions, and comparing alternative extraction options. Project is viable if NPV > 0.
common_traps: Year 0 capital cost C_0 is not discounted (or discounted with t=0 where (1+r)^0 = 1).

title: Break-Even Stripping Ratio (BESR)
variable_meanings: V = Value of 1 tonne of mineral/coal at pit top; C_mining = Production/mining cost of 1 tonne of ore; C_stripping = Cost to excavate, haul and dump 1 m3 of overburden waste.
units: m3 of waste per tonne of ore (m3/t)
when_to_use: Determining the economic depth limit where opencast mining ceases to be profitable and underground mining should be considered.
common_traps: Make sure units match (cost per tonne of ore vs cost per m3 of waste).
example_problem: V = 1500 Rs/t, C_mining = 500 Rs/t, C_stripping = 200 Rs/m3 => BESR = (1500 - 500) / 200 = 5.0 m3/tonne.
